posts.author: favalora
posts.content_md:
Hi - 

Somehow, I was invited to an "un-conference" hosted by O'Reilly, Nature, and Google this weekend at the Googleplex in Mountain View called "Science Foo 2008." About 200 people with various amplitudes of scientific, artistic, entrepreneurial, biological, etc. interest are coming for 2 days of talks on a schedule that's decided at the spur of the moment. [Here are a few photos of last year's event.](http://www.edge.org/3rd_culture/scifoo07/scifoo07_index.html) A little anxious about the incredible list of people attending!

I don't know if anyone reading this forum is going; I know several 3-D folks went last year. Anyway, I'll try to "represent" and guide a one-hour conversation about the many 3-D display technologies that've been developed over the last 1.5 centuries. I'll talk about stereoscopy, IP and lenticular displays, parallax barriers, multi-projector and view-sequential displays, volumetric... ah, yes, and a where-we're-at in holographic video. And try to dispel some myths / snake oil.

best

gregg

posts.author: Colin Kaminski
posts.content_md: Gregg, if you want to record it I can transcribe it for the wiki?

posts.content_md:
Hey, that would be fun. I think it could be problematic, though -- I don't know if they allow videotaping in there (lots of people saying off-the-record stuff), and let's just say that my slides "borrow" a lot of imagery...

-g
